messages:
Ari (PM): FYI -- I put together a short draft PRD for an "Adaptive Variant Routing" feature for the Redwood API. Goal: route requests across model variants (high-accuracy, quantized, regional replicas) by latency/cost/quality and have predictable fallbacks/rollouts. Need spec + acceptance criteria review before I turn into an RFC. Posting minimal contract + notes below. Please read & comment today if possible. :eyes:

Sam (Eng): I skimmed. Quick Q: do we change the public API shape or keep it opt-in via a header? Also what are the hard rollback semantics?

Ari (PM): opt-in param on the request payload is my preference so we don't break existing clients. If no variant available, we fallback to current stable model for that endpoint. Rollback should be automatic if error rate or latency > threshold (more on thresholds in acceptance criteria).

Jules (ML): ML note: quantized/fast variants sometimes degrade output quality for long-context chat chains. Acceptance criteria needs an eval gating step (prompt set + N metrics) and a per-customer quality delta threshold. Also rerank interactions: embeddings/rerank path must maintain a minimum NDCG@5 vs baseline.

Devon (Design): from client UX POV, minimize new fields. Proposal: optional body field `variant_hint` + `fallback_policy` enum. Default = `stable`. Example: { "variant_hint": "fast-small", "fallback_policy": "stable_then_regional" }. Docs should show examples for chat + embeddings + rerank.

Sam (Eng): putting a compact contract here. Comments welcome.

Sam (Eng): ```json
{
  "model": "redwood-chat-1",
  "variant_hint": "fast-quantized-1", // optional
  "fallback_policy": "stable_then_regional", // enum: stable|regional|none
  "route_metadata": { "region": "eu-west-1" } // optional affinity
}
```

Maya (SRE): observability rules: we need token-level latency breakdown per variant, error-rate by variant, and per-route cost estimate. Canary rollout must stream metrics to console and have auto-trips: 5xx rate > 0.5% OR p95 latency > 2x baseline for 5m window => rollback. Also note: KV cache incompatibilities between model families are a real thing; must be in edgecases.

Ari (PM): acceptance criteria draft (short):
- API contract backward compatible (existing requests unchanged).
- Gating: run eval set (chat prompts + rerank evals) on candidate variant; quality loss <= 2% relative for chat (measured by pass@k / human proxy) and NDCG@5 degradation <= 0.03 for rerank.
- Performance: p50/p95 token latency for variant in-canary within X% (TBD) vs stable.
- Safety: no increase in toxic/PII leakage alerts per eval harness (automated checks).
- Canary rollback triggers as Maya listed.
- Docs + SDK snippet updated.

QA-bot: test cases to add:
- happy path with variant_hint present -> routed correctly
- fallback when variant down -> stable model returned
- concurrency spike -> no cache corruption (session affinity tested)
- embeddings -> rerank pipeline keeps top-K ordering stable within threshold
- negative tests for malformed variant_hint

Sam (Eng): edgecases I want called out explicitly:
- Session KV cache: if a variant uses different tokenizer/k-v encoding, we must detect and clear or mark session incompatible and fallback.
- Partial responses: if variant returns truncated tokens due to OOM, we should surface as 500 and fallback.
- Cross-endpoint routing: requests that combine embeddings + chat (client does both) need atomic routing decisions or documented eventual consistency.

Jules (ML): evaluation mini-process: run 10k chat prompts + 2k rerank queries; log quality diffs and run A/B with 10% traffic for 48h before full rollout. Add a guard for long-context (>4096 tokens) where we default to high-accuracy variant.

Maya (SRE): deployment notes: schedule canary with 2% traffic -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 30m observation windows. Automation: if any auto-trip occurs, revert to previous stable and mark variant as "suspended" in routing table. Include a manual override for enterprise customers.

Devon (Design): example docs blurb: "You can hint preferred variants using optional `variant_hint`. Redwood will respect hints while maintaining safety and SLOs; if the hinted variant can't honor the request, Redwood will fallback according to `fallback_policy`." Add inline examples for completions, chat streaming, and embeddings->rerank flows.

Ari (PM): Action items:
- Sam: update contract to include `session_token_hash` detection flag + explicit error codes for fallback (owner: @Sam) :point_right: due EOD tomorrow.
- Jules: prepare eval harness thresholds for rerank NDCG and chat proxies (owner: @Jules) due in 3 days.
- Maya: add canary automation playbook + console alerts (owner: @Maya) due 2 days.
- Devon: doc snippets + SDK examples (owner: @Devon) due 4 days.
- QA: add test matrix as QA-bot suggested (owner: @QA) due next sprint.

Sam (Eng): acked. I'll add the session token detection + error codes. Quick ask: what should error code look like for fallback? `variant_unavailable` with details?

Ari (PM): yes `variant_unavailable` and `fallback_performed` in response metadata. Example response field: `{"fallback_performed": true, "fallback_reason": "kv_incompat"}`. Keep it small.

Jules (ML): +1 on fallback metadata, useful for offline analysis. Also log which eval prompt categories saw the biggest deltas.

Maya (SRE): I'll draft the automation. One more ops edge: rate limits per-variant to prevent noisy neighbor in shared dedicated pools.

Devon (Design): will do docs + copy.

Ari (PM): Thanks all. If no major objections by EOD I'll convert this into an RFC and link to the PRD. :rocket:

Sam (Eng): :thumbsup:

Jules (ML): :eyes:

Maya (SRE): noted.
